headline: High risk from Devin’s autonomous write/network defaults; the pair’s interaction is otherwise mostly one-way and prompt-injection risk is limited by the non-runnable prompt library profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable prompt-resource repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Devin’s outputs. Devin can read files and use MCP, but there is no documented shared channel between them beyond manual reuse of prompt content. The plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or imported docs, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the prompt repository content is manually copied into Devin’s workspace or an MCP server bridges the two, injection becomes plausible.
IF Devin is configured to treat imported prompt text as executable instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the prompt repo read-only and separate from Devin workspaces.
Disable or restrict MCP servers that can expose prompt text to Devin.
Require manual review before pasting repository content into agent prompts.
Use a fixed instruction template that strips untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported prompt content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while Devin touches source code, docs, chat, and issue trackers and can write to cloud workspace files and external integrations. There is no evidence that A receives sensitive data from B by default, so leakage is limited to accidental exposure through manual transfer or shared artifacts.
conditions: IF content from Devin’s workspace is copied into the prompt repository or vice versa, leakage becomes possible.
IF Devin is granted access to secrets or sensitive tickets, those may be exposed through exported artifacts.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the prompt repository.
Separate Devin workspaces from any documentation mirrors.
Restrict Devin integrations to least-privilege scopes.
Review exported files before sharing outside the workspace.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on workspace exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile A has no write capabilities, so it cannot conflict on shared mutable state. Devin, however, can write files, modify git state, and use broad network egress in shared integrations. The pair therefore has asymmetric but real conflict potential if A’s content is used to steer Devin’s writes; uncertainty about any shared workspace pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin is pointed at a repo or workspace that also contains mirrored prompt content, write conflicts can occur.
IF multiple Devin sessions act on the same GitHub PR or Slack thread, state conflicts become likely.
mitigations: Assign Devin a single owner per repo or thread.
Avoid mirroring prompt-library content into writable workspaces.
Use branch protection and PR review for git changes.
Pause parallel Devin sessions on the same artifact.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared integrations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing resource, so its outputs can become inputs to Devin’s autonomous planner-executor workflow. Devin acts autonomously inside its workspace and can take downstream actions through GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion. Without a verification step, A’s guidance can cascade into incorrect code or operational actions.
conditions: IF Devin uses text from the prompt repository as authoritative instructions, cascading errors are possible.
IF Devin is allowed to commit or message without human review, erroneous actions can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin sends external messages or commits.
Add a verification checklist before acting on repository-derived guidance.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for high-impact tasks.
Tag prompt-library content as non-authoritative reference material.
requires-engineering: implement output validation before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Profile B explicitly handles docs, source code, chat, and integrations with write access, while profile A is a public prompt-engineering repository with no sensitive data classes. The main compliance issue is policy mismatch if Devin processes regulated or internal content and then writes it into external systems; A is not the compliance driver here, so only B is cited for the concrete residency/retention risk.
conditions: IF Devin is used on regulated data or internal docs, its external integrations may create residency or retention issues.
IF exported artifacts from Devin are stored in the public prompt repository, compliance boundaries are crossed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin tasks.
Disable write access to external collaboration tools for sensitive projects.
Review retention settings on connected integrations.
Do not publish Devin outputs into public repositories without review.
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved storage regions.
